note: This is not a DQG300 certificate. Structured DQG300 evidence for each of the 299 atomic gates, independent SME judgments and source-review signoff must be completed before a PASS can be asserted.

review.bestAnswerProof: Alternative procedures retain required ventilation and tests without incorrectly treating the vapor hazard as eliminated.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.A: Ventilation controls but has not eliminated the atmospheric hazard.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.B: One initial test is insufficient to establish safe conditions throughout entry.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.D: Ventilation must continue until every entrant has left.

review.bestAnswerProof: The key isolates both the motor and feed route instead of relying on a potentially leaking valve or a local stop.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.A: A shutoff valve can leak into the vessel despite the agitator lockout.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.C: A local stop is not verified isolation of the agitator.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.D: A tagged single block valve may still leak.

review.bestAnswerProof: The key combines representative depth sampling and monitoring while exposure conditions are changing.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.A: Opening readings may miss heavier gases near the work position.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.B: Post-work tests cannot protect workers from changing conditions during entry.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.C: Oxygen-only checks omit anticipated toxic or flammable gases.

review.bestAnswerProof: The first option preserves continuous attendant capability; intermittent relays or video do not correct the stated communication gap.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.B: Scheduled radio contact leaves periods without reliable entrant communication.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.C: CCTV alone does not restore effective two-way entrant communication.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.D: Rover relay does not solve the absent dedicated attendant coverage.

review.bestAnswerProof: The key integrates both the required mechanical retrieval equipment and verified site-specific rescue capability.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.A: A general service contract does not establish timely competence for this space.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.B: Manual hauling overlooks the mechanical retrieval device required at this depth.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.D: Generic training records do not establish proficiency for the particular geometry.

review.bestAnswerProof: The key removes people, stops the source and verifies safe conditions rather than relying on an old reading or alarm reset.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.A: Increased exhaust leaves the oxygen supply leak uncontrolled.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.C: A prior test is invalid after the new oxygen release.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.D: Alarm clearance alone does not ensure source control or safe reauthorization.

review.bestAnswerProof: The key corrects the exposure source and recognizes the need for renewed coordinated hazard assessment.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.A: Extraction cannot substitute for controlling an avoidable exhaust source.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.B: Moving the source does not validate an unchanged entry assessment.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.C: One clean reading cannot establish future protection from ongoing emissions.

review.bestAnswerProof: The key includes required cancellation, reassessment and fresh authorization rather than reliance on the old permit.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.B: The original permit cannot merely be suspended for an unauthorized condition.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.C: Replacing monitoring records cannot restore invalid entry authorization.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.D: The cause and implications of the release must be reassessed.

review.bestAnswerProof: The key integrates live indicators for both atmospheric and flooding hazards, tied to an evacuation decision.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.A: A forecast does not monitor sudden changes in upstream water flow.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.C: An entry-time gas check cannot reveal gas liberated later by disturbed deposits.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.D: Ventilation cannot detect or prevent the rising-water engulfment hazard.

review.bestAnswerProof: The key anticipates a change in hazard classification before exposing personnel to newly introduced vapor.

decisiveDistractorFlaws.A: Geometry is not the only factor that determines permit classification.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.B: One check does not resolve a foreseeable vapor-generation hazard.
decisiveDistractorFlaws.D: Post-work evaluation happens after possible hazardous exposure.
